title: the sandbox that is a sandbox
intent: The PTC sandbox checks the name of the binding the model asked for and then evaluates the body the model supplied, in a plain let. The whitelist is a list of names, so a form named read can delete a file. This is the one claim that is refuted for a reason that matters: it is the mechanism that would make an Emacs Lisp agent competitive with a shell agent, and it is the mechanism that is currently unsafe. The real answer is sandbox.el, which needs Emacs 29 and later; until that exists, the boundary is a static analysis of the free symbols of the form, and anything the analysis does not understand is refused.
checks: ./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/test-yeah-state.el tests/unit/test-yeah-loop.el tests/unit/test-yeah-tools.el tests/unit/test-yeah-perm.el tests/unit/test-yeah-session.el tests/unit/test-yeah-compact.el tests/unit/test-yeah-undo.el tests/unit/test-yeah-acp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-emcp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-gptel.el tests/unit/test-yeah-subagent.el tests/unit/test-yeah-shell.el tests/unit/test-yeah-codes.el
objection: A static analysis of the free symbols of a form is a parser, and parsers have edges: a macro expands, a backquote evaluates, a funcall reaches anything. The check that the body is confined can pass while the body still reaches the host.
refuted_by: A form that reaches the host through a path the analysis does not see, run against the boundary. If such a form runs, the boundary is a description and not a boundary.
